The candidate and its receipts are unchanged. I’ll finish the read-only pass over the full diff and the owning source, using only file reads and search.The driver-selection and Comment-bit edits are in the diff. I’ll read the remaining product changes and check the new contract suite against the same rules.The per-drive driver selection is in place, but one global listing gate still opens every authoritative drive when any other profile cannot use grant narrowing.

## Verdict: FINDINGS

### High — one non-authoritative profile disables grant narrowing for every profile

`packages/core/src/Repositories/Drive/NodeReadRepository.php:508-519`

`grantFilteringApplies()` returns false when any registered profile has grants disabled or its selected driver is not grant-authoritative. Gate, Spatie, and Azgard are not (`AzgardPermissionDriver.php:69`, `SpatiePermissionDriver.php:14-16`). `PanelAccessScope::candidateNodeIds()` then returns null (`packages/filament/src/Support/PanelAccessScope.php:43-44`), and these queries stay unfiltered:

- `packages/filament/src/Resources/DriveResource.php:65-67`
- `packages/filament/src/Resources/NodeGrantResource.php:80-81`
- `packages/filament/src/Resources/NodeShareResource.php:83-84`
- `packages/filament/src/Resources/ActivityResource.php:67-68`

`constrainToAccessible()` (`NodeReadRepository.php:421-422`) does the same. The node table later exact-filters only the loaded page (`ListNodes.php:39-44`). Drive, grant, share, and activity queries do not.

Trigger: profile `hr` uses `database`, profile `eng` uses `gate`, `spatie`, or `azgard` (or `hr` stays authoritative while `eng` sets `grants(false)`). An actor with no grants on an `hr` drive still receives that drive, its grant rows, its share rows, and its activity. Before this change the boolean followed the single active driver, so an authoritative database install stayed narrowed.

Correction: build the candidate set per drive. Keep grant-anchor ids for drives whose selected driver is grant-authoritative and whose grants feature is on. Limit the open set to drives that are not. Do not let one profile turn `grantFilteringApplies()` off for the others. `PanelAccessScope` should keep a real id predicate in that mixed case.

The per-drive subject loops in `candidateNodeIds()` (`536-557`) and `sharedNodeIds()` (`AccessResolver.php:402-424`) already select the profile driver. The global boolean discards that set.

## Checked, no further defect

Comment is bit 32 and `Permission::all()` is 63, with `All` removed. Level masks are 1/33/39/47/63. `Ability::Comment` requires 32 and `Manage` requires 63. `bitsFor()` ORs the level mask at read time (`AccessResolver.php:686-688`); the raw `permissions` column is not rewritten. Reader plus stored 31 does not gain Comment. Owner does, because the level mask is now 63.

`OwnerRef` and `AccessScope` match the scoped shape. `canCreateInWorkspace` is gone from package PHP. The seven live callers call `canCreateIn(actor, $drive)`. `OperationGuard` still applies the profile policy after the ACL branch, including for system actors (`OperationGuard.php:38-40`, `55-57`). No `download(bool)` API was added.

Scalar, batch, and explain all fold role deny the same way (`AccessResolver.php:108-116`, `233-234`, `331-339`). Results are not memoized. The driver cache key is `key|class` and the class is read from config on each resolve (`PermissionDriverManager.php:62-80`). Spatie subject expansion sets the drive-owner team and restores the previous team and relations (`SpatiePermissionDriver.php:138-152`, `203-218`). Role and team grant insertion uses the node drive’s driver (`GrantNodeAccessAction.php:75`).

The public suite checks the shared allow/deny fixture and scalar, batch, and explain parity for every ability (`PermissionDriverContractTests.php:20-33`), and the core contract test runs it for database, stub, gate, and spatie. The architecture allowlist is exactly `Testing/Contracts/PermissionDriverContractTests.php` (`ArchTest.php:338-341`). Anonymous `level=commenter` is rejected on the share request (`StoreShareLinkRequest.php:37`). The public share controller still authorizes only View and Download. No anonymous comment route was added.

Latest recorded receipts for V1–V9, V80, V82, Arch, snapshots, and the isolated negative control are exit 0. This review did not re-run them.

## Non-gating limitations

- `docs/guide/permission-drivers.md`, `docs/reference/contracts.md`, `docs/reference/rest-api.md`, and `docs/guide/sharing.md` still describe `canCreateInWorkspace`, workspace fields, and mask `0..31`. The candidate’s `UPGRADE.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` carry the public delta. Those guides are outside the candidate file list.
- A share created with `level=writer`, `organizer`, or `owner` and no explicit mask stores 39/47/63, including Comment. The public share controller never checks `Ability::Comment`. Mint enforcement remains P3.4.
- The V29 edit leg is `AccessResolver::can(Edit)`, not an edit HTTP call. Commenter mask 33 does not include Update.
- `OperationGuard::tenantBoundary()` is still empty. Strict tenancy remains P3.8.
- Recorded checks cover the five impacted packages only. No whole-phase qualification is claimed.

Resuming the read-only review of PLAN2.

Shell execution and editing are disabled. I will finish reading the 2339-line diff and all candidate source files to reach a verdict.

Reading the diff in ~500-line chunks. Verifying permission masks, ability thresholds, and removed permissions against acceptance criteria.

Checking the diff against the acceptance criteria. Verifying raw mask storage, normalized level owners on read, OwnerRef and AccessScope structures, atomic removal of canCreateInWorkspace, new PermissionDriver and AccessResolver methods, driver coverage across all permission backends, and profile-selected driver behavior for grants and node checks.The diff review continues. The remaining critical source changes require inspection.

New files are absent from the diff output. I am continuing to read from line 500 onward to inspect the security-critical logic.

The diff index ends at line 1920, leaving the final 419 lines unread. New test files were located at the end of the diff. The planned review targets AccessResolver profile selection and batch grouping, PermissionDriverManager cache keys and stale config, AccessScope and OwnerRef, GrantNodeAccessAction enumerable subjects, and ConfigValidator null rejection.

The review scope now includes StoreShareLinkRequest, NodeReadRepository, OperationGuard, contract tests, the architecture allowlist, and callers.

Two specific bugs are being targeted: whether batch grouping correctly caches subjects per scope and includes nodeOwner in inner scopes, and whether resolveRole returns deny bits so drivers can properly deny access.Continuing the read-only review of the remaining diff. New files and critical logic are the current focus.

Checking PermissionDriverManager::forProfile for null driver returns and global fallback behavior. ConfigValidator appears to use a null coalescing operator for this.

Confirmed the fallback mechanism. `PermissionDriverManager::forProfile` passes a null driver key to `driver()`, which then falls back to the global permission driver via `$key ??= $this->accessConfig->permissionDriver()`.

Need to verify Profile::getPermissionDriver() returns null when unset. ConfigValidator coalesces the profile driver with the global fallback before asserting the driver implements PermissionDriver.

Checking whether `assertImplements` fails closed on empty strings to ensure missing driver classes are rejected. Also examining a potential batch grouping bug in the node loop where each node is processed individually through `storageOf` and `forProfile`.

The batch grouping logic is sound. The outer group key already includes owner_id, so the inner regrouping by drive_id and owner_id produces one group per driver. Raw owner_id in the outer key and Identity::stringify in the inner key are compatible for grouping. Now examining the subjects cache within batches.

The subjects cache is scoped to the batch and same scope, not singleton lifetime. Need to verify whether override caching is also limited to this scope.

A behavior change was spotted: previously non-allow decisions were skipped, but now deny decisions contribute denied bits. The spec requires preserving existing deny/inherit equivalence.

The old code comment clarifies that role lanes primarily contribute allows, while ACL deny serves as the final unoverrideable veto. The new code ORs roleDeniedBits into deniedBits. This raises a question about whether the change is intentional per P3-design or a behavior change that breaks the existing deny/inherit equivalence. The user's request to verify scalar and batch deny/inherit parity is central to resolving this.

OPUS S6 explicitly restricts the role lane to raising allow decisions. A deny decision from the role driver should therefore not act as a veto. Treating Decision::isDeny() as a veto bit in the new code violates this contract and breaks the intended deny/inherit equivalence.

Re-examining the scope wording: "grants disabled исключает ACL lane но не role denial." This suggests host role driver denials should still apply when grants are disabled. The effectiveGrants path needs inspection to verify this distinction.

The full AccessResolver must be read to confirm grants-disabled behavior and whether role denials from resolve() are a new addition.

Spatie subjectsForIn sets team id before calling subjectsFor. Need to verify that subjectsFor uses the current team context and restores relations correctly. If getRoleNames() is team-scoped, this is valid.

The outer batch grouping key includes drive id, profile, driver class, and node owner. This means subjects are fetched per group when different scopes in one batch use different teams.

The batch grouping key omits the team identifier. Each drive has a single owner, so the team is constant within a group and this is not a bug. subjectsFor is called once per evaluateGroup using the scope of nodes[0].

sharedNodeIds scans all drives via cursor. This diverges from the global subjects approach and may violate the profile-selected driver requirement.

A potential bug was spotted: sharedNodeIds calls AccessScope::forDrive($drive) without passing a node owner. Spatie team resolution uses driveOwner id, which is correct for team context. However, if role subjects depend on node owner, shared listing could miss owner-dependent roles.

The specification requires batch and scalar outputs to be identical, including owner-dependent roles. Because sharedNodeIds calls forDrive without passing a node owner, it cannot satisfy this requirement. This is a concrete behavior bug.

candidateNodeIds likely repeats the same owner-dependent subjects bug. The next step is to inspect test fixtures and ProfilePermissionDriverTest.

The PermissionDriverManager cache key combines the driver key with the configuration class string. This prevents stale resolved drivers when config remaps a key to a different class at runtime.

The cache key change prevents stale driver identity, but it does not guarantee the driver's internal AccessConfig is not stale. If AccessConfig snapshots configuration at construction time, remapping permissions inside the driver could produce outdated results. The specification only guards against returning a stale resolved driver object, not against stale internal state.

ProfileRegistry is instantiated on every `forProfile` call rather than cached, which keeps the profile-to-driver mapping fresh. The driver instance itself is still cached by `driver()`. If profiles are frozen at boot, runtime changes to a profile's driver mapping may be ignored. The test that modifies config driver mapping must be examined to confirm this behavior.

A ConfigValidator bug was also flagged.

ConfigValidator calls `assertImplements` with an empty string when a profile driver is missing. If that assertion does not throw on empty input, the subsequent `is_a` check on `$drivers[$profileKey]` will trigger an undefined index error. The validator must either guard against missing keys or ensure the assertion rejects empty strings.

The `is_a` check in ConfigValidator is safe because configuration typically stores class strings. The next step is to read the GrantLevel.php diff to verify mask encoding and normalization. Stored raw masks remain unchanged; levels are normalized on read. Anonymous commenter rejection was spotted in StoreShareLinkRequest. An arch allowlist pins Testing/Contracts to a single file.Continuing the diff review from line 1885, with particular attention to new files.

About 450 lines remain in the diff. The `candidateNodeIds` function is a key concern: `$anchors` changed from a collection to an array of rows, so I must verify whether subsequent code still calls collection methods on it. Unchanged lines may hide bugs.

`grantFilteringApplies` now returns false if any profile is not grant-authoritative. Previously it checked only the global driver. This conservative change may be intentional.

Need to determine whether a false `grantFilteringApplies` result skips the SQL candidate filter or bypasses ACL entirely.

`sharedNodeIds` iterates all drives. If `nodeIdsSharedWith` is global, filtering by drive_id is correct.

The role deny bits may incorrectly change deny/inherit equivalence. The original comment stated that the role lane can only raise allow and cannot override deny.

The new code ORs role deny bits into the decision path. This violates the OPUS requirement that role lanes may only raise allow and cannot override deny. A driver returning a deny Decision is now treated as a veto.

The old code ignored Decision denys entirely. This is a behavior change. I need to check whether built-in drivers ever return deny decisions. If only test drivers do, the new behavior may be intentional.

The requirement that role denial survive when grants are disabled is confirmed. I will now inspect `effectiveGrants` and the `ConfigValidator` driver key checks. The `forProfile` null driver fallback to global is correct. I also need to verify whether `PermissionDriverManager` cache handles class changes from `classFor`.

Need to verify whether `classFor` reads configuration live.

`subjectsFor` now correctly issues two subject calls for two scopes. The batch cache is per evaluateGroup.

Must confirm that `EvaluateMany` override counts remain three and that overrides are cached per scope rather than per node. Role denial must apply identically in batch mode.

The `candidateNodeIds` source continuation is critical and must be read.

Also need to search for `->bits()` usage in grant resolution to check level normalization on read.

StoreShareLinkRequest permits permissions up to 63, which includes the comment bit. The scope explicitly rejects the commenter level and forbids raw comment bits from enabling anonymous commenting. I need to verify whether a public share comment endpoint exists that could exploit this raw permission.

The user clarified that the public share mint validation is P3.4 and not executed here. The candidate already rejects anonymous Commenter at the HTTP share request boundary. I must verify that no anonymous comment endpoint was added and that existing public shares do not interpret the raw comment bit as allowing comments.

I need to search for any public endpoint that checks share.permissions for comment access. The permission bitmask was raised from 31 to 63, so the raw comment bit can now be stored and might enable anonymous commenting if an endpoint treats it as a valid permission.

The bitmask values are correct. Share and Delete are absent as required. Organizer is 47, Owner is 63, Commenter is 33, and Reader is 1.

A raw permissions value of 31 no longer satisfies Manage. Owner level normalization on read expands stored Owner to 63, so existing Owner entries remain valid. However, a raw permissions=31 stored without an Owner level would fail to satisfy Manage. The spec explicitly forbids silent backfill of raw31 to 63.

The read formula `level->bits() | permissions` confirms that a null level paired with raw permissions=31 would still fail to satisfy Manage. I need to verify whether this storage mode actually exists.

Ability::Comment now requires permission bit 32, so Readers cannot comment and Writers can.

Filament NodeResource has two call sites.

The second Filament NodeResource call site still needs to be located in the remaining diff.

New files at the end of the diff require inspection.

If `grantFilteringApplies` returns false because any profile is non-authoritative, the SQL candidate optimization is disabled globally. This could be conservative, but it might also force exact evaluation or leak nodes. The caller must be checked to confirm the actual behavior.

An empty profile registry is another edge case: if `all()` is empty, the loop never runs and returns true, which could incorrectly apply candidate filtering even when no profiles exist.

`forProfile` instantiates `ProfileRegistry` via the container on every drive call. This is not a correctness bug.

Spatie `setPermissionsTeamId` accepts string ULIDs for the scope owner ID. This matches the previous `workspaceId` behavior and is acceptable.

`OwnerRef::ofModel` needs verification of its morph class or key.

AccessScope::forDrive reads the drive owner from owner_type, owner_id, and tenant_id. The spec requires the owner model reference to use getMorphClass or getMorphKey. If owner_type already stores the morph alias, using the column is correct. OwnerRef::ofModel must be checked to confirm it matches the persisted morph. The node owner remains owner_id.

The node owner subject type uses `storage->owner_type` rather than the morph alias. This appears to be pre-existing code, not a new bug introduced by the diff.

ConfigValidator correctly falls back to an empty string when a profile key maps to null or is missing from the drivers array. This ensures the subsequent `assertImplements` check rejects invalid driver classes. I still need to verify whether `is_a` could bypass that validation for some invalid values.

Batch role denial parity is confirmed: `evaluateGroup` applies the `roleDenied` flag.

`explain` also applies the `roleDenied` flag. I still need to read `evaluateGroup` fully to confirm that batch override caching is per scope rather than a singleton. The `PermissionDriverManager` cache is safe because `classFor` reads live configuration before lookup, so stale driver classes are not cached.

The Profile registry may be frozen. If Profile objects are built once from config at first resolution, later changes to the permission_drivers map or the profile's driver key could leave forProfile returning stale data. I need to read ProfileRegistry and the relevant test.

The V29 deny-veto test grants Reader with Effect::Deny and permissions 32. It is unclear whether the deny mask uses level bits or explicit permissions. The V2 NodeCommentApiTest passed, so the implementation likely respects the explicit permission bit.

The deny-veto test passes, but the underlying code path in AclFolder/apply must be inspected to confirm it correctly applies the explicit permissions bit. The candidateNodeIds method also needs its remaining implementation read.

The sharedNodeIds method iterates all drives without tenant scoping. This is pre-existing behavior from the prior global subject query, not a new cross-tenant leak. Strict tenancy is deferred to P3.8, so this does not constitute a finding.Documentation still references canCreateInWorkspace and allBits.

The scope explicitly includes snapshots/docs. UPGRADE.md and CHANGELOG.md are task files. The docs directory is also in scope.

`snapshots/docs` likely refers to public API snapshots and the candidate's own changelog/upgrade files, not the full docs site. The task files only cover UPGRADE.md and CHANGELOG.md. Stale documentation outside this scope is a non-gating limitation.

Stale docs are a known drift, not a gating finding. The item's deliverables are public reusable contract tests and UPGRADE/CHANGELOG, which remain intact.

The review is shifting from documentation to hunting real bugs in critical source sections. The first target is candidateNodeIds continuation.

The candidateNodeIds diff only replaced the start of the method. The remainder must be read to confirm whether `$anchors` is now an array and if later code calls collection methods on it.

grantFilteringApplies returns false globally if any profile is not grant-authoritative. A host with both a non-authoritative gate profile and a database profile would therefore bypass grant filtering entirely.

Role denial when grants are disabled is intentional. The spec says grants disabled excludes the ACL lane but not role denial, and the test locks this new behavior. This is not a bug.

ProfileAllowDriver returns ALLOW Owner when nodeOwner is null, because id === 2 evaluates to false.

The remap test configures the positive driver to ProfileDenyDriver.

The remap test relies on a live config read. `classFor` must resolve the new driver class dynamically, and `forProfile` should look up the "positive" key to fetch the updated driver. A potential bug is flagged: `ProfileRegistry` is resolved via the container inside `forProfile`, which may bypass the singleton instance.

The ProfileRegistry singleton concern is resolved: `forProfile` calls `make()` on every invocation, so it always returns the current bound instance.

Next targets are `classFor` cache staleness, whether `candidateNodeIds` now returns an array instead of a collection, and whether `sharedWith` delegates to `sharedNodeIds`.

A new test verifies that the S3 parts controller gates requests through the profile driver, expecting a 403 when create permission is denied.

The S3 parts controller test passed, confirming the endpoint checks canCreateIn and returns 403 when denied. The test sequence—initiating S3 before installing the create gate—ensures the driver is remapped after the session exists, so the 403 is not a false positive from auth or missing session. Next target is the Filament create-disabled profile.

The guidance for NodeResourceCreateGateTest specifies testing both canCreateIn branches in NodeResource, covering allow, deny, and a create-disabled profile. The test only covers the gate allow/deny paths, not the create-disabled profile feature itself.

The "allow/deny/create-disabled profile" requirement likely means the deny case is the create-disabled profile, not a separate feature flag. The new NodeResourceCreateGateTest should cover both canCreateIn branches and this deny path.

The NodeResourceCreateGateTest already covers the create-disabled profile case through its deny branch, so no third test is missing. The next step is to verify OperationGuard still enforces profile restrictions after the canCreateIn rename. Because this item depends on P3.6, the profile wiring should remain intact.

OperationGuard must be read to confirm it still invokes the profile policy after the rename.

ConfigValidator has a bug when a driver key is missing: `assertImplements` and the surrounding validate method do not handle empty strings or invalid keys. The production test covers null driver rejection for selected profiles, but a profile whose `getPermissionDriver()` returns null may fall back to the global null driver.

The null-driver fallback in ConfigValidator may already be covered by the existing global null check in production. The per-profile null-key case still needs verification.

A new concern is grant level normalization. Reader with raw permissions 31 cannot comment, but Owner with the same raw value can. This implies the read path ORs level bits rather than using raw stored values. The code must be checked to confirm this behavior and ensure it does not write back normalized bits.

The ORing of level bits is confirmed correct: Reader with raw 31 cannot comment, while Owner with the same raw value can.

A new concern is share commenter validation. The candidate rejects Commenter at the HTTP boundary, but if permissions=32 is minted without a level, the raw bit may still be set. I need to check whether public share or comment endpoints use share.permissions & Comment.

PermissionDriverContractTests is a thin assertion helper. The existing PermissionDriverContractTest calls it, but it is unclear whether it runs for every driver type. The test file decisionsOver adds the contract assert, so the driver iteration scope needs verification.

A potential batch subject scope bug was spotted in evaluateGroup: the outer grouping key includes owner_id.

The batch subject scope concern is resolved. Subjects are computed once for the first node in each group, then re-grouped by drive and owner. ProfileAllowDriver resolves roles using the node owner from the scope passed to resolveRole, not from subjectsFor. This preserves owner-dependent role decisions across the batch.

The batch subject scope concern is resolved. The outer grouping key includes owner_id, so nodes with different owners are kept in separate groups and inner scopes remain distinct.

A new potential issue was spotted: `forProfile` caches driver instances by both key and class. Two profiles that map to the same driver class but use different keys could incorrectly share a cached instance.

The shared driver instance concern is resolved. The Spatie driver is stateless and sets its team per call, so sharing one instance across profiles is safe. Caching by key and class also prevents stale instances if the container singleton is rebound.

The `forProfile` method falls back to the global default driver when a profile returns null, and missing keys throw with fail-closed behavior. The next unread targets are `candidateNodeIds` and `sharedWith`.

The S3 parts controller will be inspected to confirm the 403 is driven by a real canCreateIn gate rather than a false positive. The Filament folderOptions test expects non-empty results when allow is true.

The Filament folderOptions test passed, confirming non-empty results when allowed. ProfileCreateGate replaces the entire ProfileRegistry with only the default profile, but this is test-only and safe.

ProfileCreateGate hardcodes `vaulter.manage` as always true. This super-ability override does not bypass `canCreateIn`, which remains gated by `vaulter.create`. The DriveResource create flag correctly requires both the ability and `canCreateIn`.

The root abilitiesFor path uses effective grants. The super-ability override grants Create when allowed, but canCreateIn still gates the endpoint against the allow flag. Document creation tests passed, confirming that 201 responses require both the ability and canCreateIn.

Two new potential bugs were spotted.

`grantFilteringApplies` may return false when any profile is non-authoritative. This would either leak all nodes or force exact evaluation. The code must be read to confirm the behavior.

`candidateNodeIds` filters anchors to the drive after fetching grants across all nodes. A role subject on one profile could match grants on another profile's nodes if the same subject ID exists.

The cross-profile anchor leak is resolved. Drive_id filtering excludes grants from other drives, so role:7 anchors on the database drive do not leak into the role drive's candidate set. The test expectation that b is absent from candidates is confirmed.

`sharedNodeIds` is also global and filtered by drive, so cross-drive leaks are blocked there too. The cursor performance across all drives is a performance issue, not a security bug. `OwnerRef` treats empty strings as invalid but allows integer 0 and string "0" as valid IDs per the specification.

The Node owner Subject type uses the storage owner_type rather than the node owner morph. This is a pre-existing pattern that ProfileAllowDriver handles by checking only the ID, and it was not introduced by this diff. The next unread target is scopeFor.

The SpatiePermissionDriver instanceof check in PermissionDriverManager is safe. Subclasses that expose subjectsForIn will still match, and decoration edge cases are not demonstrated.

Team ID type handling is pre-existing: driveOwner->id may be a string, but the driver already accepts int|string.

A potential relation restore bug was spotted in subjectsForIn inside the withTeam closure.

The `subjectsForIn` relation restore is safe. The actor's roles and permissions are unbound before the team-scoped query runs, then restored afterward via nested try/finally blocks. Tests already cover both restores.

The actor's relations are restored to saved state. Tests already cover this. A potential permission cache leak was noted if Spatie stores permissions in a property outside relations. The existing resolve() path restores team and relations too. I should read withTeam and resolve to compare. I also need to verify whether subjectsFor calls setPermissionsTeamId again inside the withTeam wrapper.

Direct driver->subjectsFor() calls bypass the withTeam wrapper and leak team scope. AccessResolver and NodeReadRepository both route through manager->subjectsFor(), but other paths may still call the driver directly.

Direct driver->subjectsFor calls in tests are acceptable. The remaining concern is whether any production path still bypasses the manager and calls the driver directly.

Role grant insertion uses forProfile and enumeratesRoleSubjects. Spatie implements EnumeratesRoleSubjects, but ProfileRoleSubjectsDriver extends DatabasePermissionDriver. The test expects a role grant on the roles profile to succeed while throwing UnenumerableGrantSubjectException on the default database profile.A significant potential bug was found in evaluateGroup subject caching.

The outer evaluateMany groups nodes by drive, profile, driver class, and owner_id. Each evaluateGroup call therefore receives nodes with identical owner_ids. The inner regrouping by drive_id and owner_id is redundant.

The caching logic is sound. Because the outer group already isolates nodes by owner_id, fetching subjects once from nodes[0] covers all nodes in that group correctly.

The outer grouping key uses the raw owner_id, while the inner regrouping stringifies it. This type mismatch could cause the two levels to split nodes incorrectly.

The equivalence test now expects two subject calls for two storages. This suggests the spec may require per-storage subject resolution rather than a single shared cache per scope.

The subject call counts in the equivalence test match the implementation, so the caching logic is correct.

The bitsFor normalization was not introduced by this diff. It likely reflects a pre-existing change where level owner now returns 63 from bits(), while raw stored permissions remain unchanged.

The bitsFor comment is slightly stale but the code behavior is correct. Reader plus raw 31 yields 31, so comment permission remains blocked. Owner plus 31 yields 63, allowing comment. Old Owner grants stored as level Owner now correctly include Manage because level bits() returns 63.

Raw permissions 31 correctly deny Manage because they lack the required bit 63. The spec intentionally avoids backfilling raw 31.

grantFilteringApplies returns true when no profiles are registered. This causes listing to filter by candidates instead. A drive with a non-authoritative driver may then be skipped during candidate resolution.

A security bug was identified in grantFilteringApplies. If any registered profile is non-authoritative, the method returns false and opens the listing for all profiles, including authoritative ones. This exposes nodes that grant filtering would normally hide. The doc comment confirms this behavior is intentional to prevent grant-id constraints from wrongly hiding role-allowed nodes.

The security concern is mitigated by the per-node fallback. If grant filtering is disabled, queryForUser still evaluates each node individually. This prevents any node from being wrongly hidden while only slowing the listing.

The open-listing behavior is a behavior change from the previous single-driver model to a global-AND across all profiles. Candidate paths select drivers per profile, so grant filtering now applies universally rather than per profile. The exact gate logic in queryForUser and constrainToAccessible still needs review.

SQL narrowing is disabled when any profile uses gate, trading performance for safety. The exact per-node check remains the fallback. A drive with a registry-unregistered profile is unlikely to be a real issue. Empty profiles correctly enable filtering because production defaults to a single database profile.

The exact evaluation fallback remains active when grant filtering is globally disabled. This confirms the mixed-profile behavior is a conservative SQL optimization trade-off rather than a security leak.

The caller must be checked to confirm that disabling grant filtering does not bypass ability checks entirely. A database-only drive in a mixed deployment would otherwise leak nodes.

The evaluateGroup subject scope bug is now being re-examined. The outer grouping key includes both owner_id and drive id, which may affect how subjects are resolved across multiple scopes.

The evaluateGroup subject scope concern is resolved. Each group contains exactly one drive and one owner, so nodes[0] is representative for that scope. Driver class collisions across profiles are prevented because each group is keyed by drive id. All nodes in a group share the same scope, so nodes[0] is always present.

Spatie subjects depend on the drive owner team, which is already captured by the drive id in the outer grouping key. ProfileRoleSubjectsDriver subjects are scope-independent.

Scalar and batch subject resolution for Spatie are equivalent when the node owner differs but the team is identical, because both paths resolve against the same drive owner.

A potential issue was noted: sharedNodeIds constructs AccessScope::forDrive without including the node owner.

Spatie subjects are bound to the drive owner, not the node owner. Shared listings use drive-level scope and cannot know the node owner before loading nodes. This means candidate and shared paths may miss or over-include nodes that depend on node-owner-specific roles. ProfileAllowDriver resolves roles using the node owner, but its subjectsFor method still returns actor-level subjects from the Database parent.

filterSharedWith re-resolves subjects with full scope including node owner, so owner-dependent role decisions are applied at filter time. sharedNodeIds may therefore over-include candidates.

candidateNodeIds does not re-resolve. It is a superset for SQL narrowing. Owner-dependent role ALLOW decisions that lack a grant anchor would be excluded from candidates when grant filtering applies.

ProfileAllowDriver explicitly sets isGrantAuthoritative to false, confirming the driver intentionally relies on resolve() for extra access rather than grant rows. This validates the documented contract that grants are sole authority. The new behavior is therefore consistent with the driver's design.

A caller must be checked to confirm that disabling grant filtering does not bypass ability checks entirely. A real bug was identified in evaluateGroup when a group contains multiple drives.

The outer grouping key includes the drive id, so multiple drives cannot be merged into a single evaluateGroup. Role denials are applied after ACL folding and act as absolute vetoes on the final mask. They cannot be pierced by a nearer allow in the ACL chain.

Absolute role denials preserve the existing deny/inherit equivalence. Scalar and batch resolution both apply denied bits to the final mask, so parity is maintained. This behavior extends beyond the OPUS specification that resolve() only raises allow, but it is explicitly required by the item scope. The test locks deniedBits 63, confirming this is an accepted addition rather than a finding.

When grants are disabled, the ACL lane is excluded but role allow bits remain active. This keeps the role lane independent from ACL and aligns with the spec that only role denial is preserved. A host might expect grants disabled to mean no access at all.

The spec does not require role allows to be removed when grants are disabled, so the remaining role allow bits are acceptable. Scalar and batch resolution both skip ACL and apply role deny, and the test already validates deniedBits 63 for both paths. The batch subject equivalence test is being checked to confirm that per-scope subjects are resolved correctly across multiple owner groups.
